facts.fact: The Mariana Trench is located in the western Pacific Ocean and reaches a maximum depth of 10,935 metres.
Entering cold water triggers cold shock within 2 minutes, causing uncontrolled gasping.
Drowning occurs when the nose and mouth are submerged, preventing breathing.
Hydrostatic pressure increases during descent, shrinking flexible gas-filled spaces.
Increasing pressure deforms tissues and squeezes internal gas-filled organs like lungs and sinuses.
At the bottom of the trench, water pressure is over 1,000 times the standard sea level pressure.

sentences.text: What would happen to your body if you fell into the Mariana Trench?
You drop into the western Pacific Ocean, directly above a depth of 10,935 metres.
Cold water triggers cold shock and uncontrolled gasping, which can kill within 2 minutes.
With your mouth submerged, gasping forces water in and causes drowning.
As your body sinks deeper, rising hydrostatic pressure shrinks flexible gas-filled spaces.
This difference in pressure causes injuries to gas-containing internal organs like your lungs and ears.
In short, cold shock and drowning can kill you in minutes.
As you descend, rising water pressure can injure your gas-containing internal organs.
Would you ever dare to explore the ocean deeps?

title: What Happens If You Fall Into the Mariana Trench?
